subject: Science
chapter: Cell: The Building Block of Life
central_question: How do cells, as the basic structural and functional units of life, organise their boundaries, internal parts, growth, division, and continuity?
in_scope_units: Cells as the basic level of life, including unicellular and multicellular organisation into tissues, organs, and organ systems
2.1 How to Study Cells: limits of unaided vision, resolution, magnification, light microscopes, electron microscopes, and estimating cell size
2.2 Structure of a Cell: the cell boundary and exchange with the surroundings
2.2.1 Cell membrane: selective permeability, diffusion, osmosis, solution concentration, and the fluid-mosaic model
2.2.2 Cell wall: rigidity, permeability, cellulose, support, and differences between plant and animal cells
2.3 The Cell Interior: plasma membrane, cytoplasm, nucleus, organelles, and comparison of bacterial, plant, and animal cells
Prokaryotic and eukaryotic cells: nucleoid, membrane-bound nucleus, membrane-bound organelles, and typical size ranges
2.3.1 Need for organelles: coordinated division of work inside eukaryotic cells
Nucleus, chromosomes, chromatin, DNA, genes, nucleolus, and the nucleoid of prokaryotic cells
Ribosomes, rough and smooth endoplasmic reticulum, Golgi apparatus, and lysosomes
Mitochondria, cellular respiration, ATP, cristae, and energy supply
Plastids: chloroplasts, chromoplasts, leucoplasts, chlorophyll, food synthesis, colour, and storage
Vacuoles: cell sap, storage, internal pressure, support, and wilting
2.4 How Normal Cells Grow and Divide: onion root-tip observations, cell growth, and the cell cycle
2.4.1 Cell division: mitosis, meiosis, growth, repair, reproduction, chromosome number, variation, and errors in division
Cell culture and the controlled growth of cells outside the body
2.5 Cell Theory: contributions of Schleiden, Schwann, and Virchow and the three classical statements
2.5.1 Cell lifespan and growth control: contact inhibition, uncontrolled division, tumours, and programmed cell death
banned_topics: Detailed names and events of the individual stages of mitosis or meiosis, which the chapter states will be studied in higher grades
Detailed human reproductive anatomy, gamete formation, and fertilisation beyond the brief links made to Chapter 11
Detailed biochemical pathways of photosynthesis or cellular respiration beyond the organelle-level roles stated in this chapter
Taxonomic classification of bacteria, fungi, viruses, viroids, or prions beyond the brief cell-structure comparison given here
Cancer diagnosis, treatment, staging, or genetics beyond the chapter's explanation of uncontrolled cell division and tumours

known_pitfalls.claim: Magnification and resolution mean the same thing.
known_pitfalls.correction: Magnification makes an object appear larger, whereas resolution is the measure of clarity and the ability to distinguish closely spaced details.

known_pitfalls.claim: Osmosis is the movement of any solute from high concentration to low concentration.
known_pitfalls.correction: Osmosis is the diffusion of water across a selectively permeable membrane; diffusion is the net movement of particles from higher to lower concentration and can occur without a membrane.

known_pitfalls.claim: The cell wall is selectively permeable like the cell membrane.
known_pitfalls.correction: The cell membrane is selectively permeable, while the rigid cell wall is permeable to water and some dissolved minerals.

known_pitfalls.claim: Animal cells shrink in concentrated sugar solution because they have a cell wall.
known_pitfalls.correction: Animal cells lack a cell wall, so water loss by osmosis causes the whole cell to shrink; in plant cells the rigid wall keeps the outer shape while the inner content shrinks.

known_pitfalls.claim: All cells have a well-defined nucleus.
known_pitfalls.correction: Prokaryotic cells lack a membrane-bound nucleus; their genetic material lies in a nucleoid. Eukaryotic cells have a well-defined nucleus.
Ribosomes are tiny sites of protein synthesis found free in the cytoplasm or attached to rough endoplasmic reticulum; the chapter does not describe them as membrane-bound.

known_pitfalls.claim: SER carries ribosomes and makes proteins.
known_pitfalls.correction: RER has ribosomes and is mainly involved in protein synthesis and secretion; SER lacks ribosomes and is involved in synthesis and storage of fats and hormones.

known_pitfalls.claim: All plastids are green and perform photosynthesis.
known_pitfalls.correction: Chloroplasts contain chlorophyll and perform photosynthesis, chromoplasts contain other coloured pigments, and leucoplasts are colourless food-storage plastids.

known_pitfalls.claim: Mitosis and meiosis produce the same number and type of daughter cells.
known_pitfalls.correction: Mitosis produces two genetically identical daughter cells with the same chromosome number, while meiosis is a two-step division that produces four gametes with half the chromosome number.
Normal cells divide in a controlled way and have a definite life span; loss of growth control can lead to uncontrolled division and tumours.
